Past analyses of AMZN (most recent first):

[2026-09-23 | AMZN | Underweight | -0.0% | +0.6% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AMZN: reduce existing exposure to 0.75x standard allocation at market (249.27) rather than parking the bulk of the trim behind the 255.00 shelf — this desk's own record (GOOGL 09-16: "place the entire reduction at market and drop the ladder"; AAPL 09-16: above-spot gates went unfilled while the call was right) shows that ladders above price convert a correct call into unexecuted risk. Execute in three pieces: ~25-33% of the position at market now, a second piece into 253.20-254.00, and the remainder into 255.00-256.30 on a rejection candle or failed intraday reclaim, with a hard time/price fallback that completes any unfilled portion on a failed bounce below 253.20 or within 5-10 sessions, ending at 0.50x. No new capital at 249-251, no short, no leverage; a daily close below 240.63 (with the 239.82 gap edge) takes residual exposure to minimum/zero, and re-adding requires a close above 256.29 on >40M shares with the MACD histogram turning positive, then a close above 259.50 or Q3 evidence of positive FCF with capex/revenue at or below 27%. Horizon 1-3 months, re-scored on the Q3 print or on the 256.29 / 240.63 triggers.

**Investment Thesis**: Direction was not the hard question — all three risk seats, the Research Manager and the trader land on reducing exposure — so the decision turns on how much to sell, on what execution rules, and why not Sell or Hold. On all three, the evidence favors a committed but partial de-risk.

WHAT IS UNREFUTED AND FORBIDS SELL. The bull's operating ledger survived every seat: revenue +19.6% to $200.6B, operating income +43.3%, operating margin +230bp to 13.7%, H1 operating cash flow +44.2% to $71.4B, $176.1B of cash and securities, ~20.9x interest coverage, and margin expansion achieved while D&A ran at 2.71x-rising capex. The primary structure is intact: the 200 SMA at 240.63 is rising, price sits 3.59% above it, and the 50 SMA remains above the 200. Even the bear concedes the business is excellent. That rules out Sell as an exit or an outright short, and this book's record is explicit that heavy de-risking inside an intact rising 50/200 structure (07-22 to 07-30) forfeited 12-22% of five-day alpha. A real core stays.

WHY NOT HOLD. The bear's tape work went completely unanswered by the conservative seat, which endorsed it: a 249.27 close below the 10 EMA (253.23), VWMA (253.54), Bollinger mid (255.18) and 50 SMA (256.29); a -2.24% session on 44.21M shares (~1.27x average) closing in the bottom quarter of the 247.76-253.99 range; MACD at -1.671 below its -1.382 signal with the histogram re-widening to -0.288; RSI 44.07 making lower highs and not oversold; five lower highs from the 284.02 close on 8/03 with the 9/21 bounce rejected at 259.49; and a VWMA that has fallen 272.05 (8/20) to 253.54 while sitting above price, meaning every recent volume cohort is underwater overhead supply. The 50 SMA has crossed five times in ten sessions — that is distribution, not support. The 09-11 reflection in this name already logged the operative lesson: with negative MACD and a sequence of lower lows, a benchmark-weight Hold mechanically produces roughly -1% alpha when the tape drifts; if the desk expects the distribution phase to resolve lower, the honest expression is a modest underweight, not a Hold padded with conditional adds.

WHY UNDERWEIGHT AND NOT A DEEPER CUT. The fundamental cautions are real but they argue for size, not exit: TTM FCF -$11.6B and H1 FCF -$27.0B on TTM capex of $173.0B (27% of revenue, 2.71x D&A) with the depreciation wave still ahead, not behind; the "FCF inflection" from -$18.2B (Q1) to -$8.8B (Q2) is one quarter helped by deferred taxes and payables/receivables timing; the $650B contractual-obligation figure reads as purchase/capacity/power commitments rather than contracted customer backlog, so the bull inverts its cash-flow direction; lease-adjusted net debt of roughly $67B once $96.3B of operating leases are included, with debt up 93% in six months and net interest income flipping negative. Earnings quality compounds it: ~68% of H1 pretax income came from non-cash marks on a $122.3B non-marketable equity book, and adjusted EPS of $2.17 versus reported $5.75 means anyone underwriting AMZN on trailing earnings is 30-45% wrong on the denominator. None of this is solvency stress, and none of it justifies abandoning the name — it justifies a smaller position carried with a re-entry ladder.

WHERE EACH SEAT WINS, AND THE TRADER'S PLAN I OVERRIDE. The aggressive seat wins the tape read and loses the arithmetic and the ambition. His "2.9:1" from 256 rests on a 260 stop that is only 0.66-0.82 ATR away at a 6.06 ATR while the 50 SMA has crossed five times in ten sessions — that is a coin flip dressed as a ratio, as the conservative and neutral both demonstrated. His proposed overweight at 260 is refused: a close above 259.50 invalidates the bearish case but does not establish a new uptrend, with the 38.2% retrace near 260.7 and the upper Bollinger at 264.60 — going overweight at resistance is buying confirmation before the evidence is complete. I also do not credit his assumption that the coiled ATR (down 39% since 8/03) resolves down; contraction is directionally silent. The conservative seat wins the risk process and supplies the two amendments I adopt: 260 is an invalidation/re-add trigger rather than a loss stop on a short, the re-add caps at standard weight, and the ladder must carry a time stop so the limit order does not become an excuse to stay heavy. The neutral seat wins the sizing: immediate move to 0.75x, roughly 0.60x into the shelf, 0.50x only on a clear rejection or if the caller is oversized — I adopt that rather than the conservative's automatic 0.50x, because a default halving overtrims a business compounding operating income 43%. What I override in all three is execution: the trader's 255.00 entry (and the neutral's 0.60x shelf target) leans too hard on a bounce the distribution read says is unlikely, and the "mid-range selling is the worst risk/reward" argument applies to a directional short, not to cutting existing exposure. The 09-16 GOOGL reflection is directly on point, so a substantial market tranche is mandatory now and the 253-256 shelf is a bonus fill, not the primary vehicle.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT. Upgrade to Hold on a daily close above 256.29 on volume >40M with the MACD histogram turning positive and price beginning to hold the 50 SMA; Overweight only on a close above 259.50 plus Q3 evidence of durably positive FCF with capex/revenue at or below 27% and the obligation ladder disclosed as backed by customer revenue contracts. Add downside: a close below 244.30 on >45M shares cuts residual to 0.40-0.50x (do not add directional downside risk there — a gap-fill bounce off 240.63/239.82 is a live possibility), and a daily close below 240.63 invalidates the bull's own primary-trend support and takes residual exposure to minimum or zero. Unconditionally, any markdown against the $122.3B equity book or a capex guide-up paired with AWS deceleration is a size-reduction event, not a dip to buy.

STATED GAPS. No portfolio, holdings, cost basis or cash was provided, so all sizing is expressed as a fraction of the caller's existing AMZN position and standard allocation, and AMZN must be counted inside the caller's aggregate AI-capex exposure alongside any NVDA/GOOGL/hyperscaler positions. No options pricing or implied volatility, so no hedge is priced — cash is the hedge. No verified earnings calendar for the Q3 print. No AWS segment revenue, margin or backlog, so the demand side of the capex program remains inference. No valuation multiple or consensus estimate. The news sample is thin and partly unverified: the Muse/Shopify read-across is sector-tape inference, and the Prime headline has no established facts — neither carries sizing weight. The price sample begins 2026-02-20, so no 52-week or multi-year reference levels exist.

**Price Target**: 244.0

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, re-scored on the Q3 print or on the 256.29 reclaim / 240.63 break triggers, whichever comes first

REFLECTION:
The 5-day window produced -0.0% raw against +0.6% alpha versus SPY, meaning AMZN marginally outperformed a down tape — a mild adverse tick for an Underweight call, but far too short to adjudicate a 1-3 month de-risking thesis built on distribution resolving lower. What it does test is the near-term tape read: the bearish EMA/VWMA stack and re-widening MACD histogram did not produce the immediate downside follow-through the trim was timed around, though the 253.20-256.30 shelf would not have filled and the market tranche remains the correct execution lesson. Next time, note explicitly that a +0.6% relative move over five sessions is inside noise for a position sized at 0.75x, and do not let a single short window update the structural calls around 256.29 or 240.63.

[2026-09-22 | AMZN | Underweight | -3.3% | -2.1% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN is Underweight: trim 40–50% of a standard full-weight position into the 254–256 area now (lean to 50–60% if the caller is concentrated or above target), leaving a 50–60% core. No new buying at 254.98 — price sits below the 20 SMA (255.77) and 50 SMA (256.26) after a third rejection at the 259 shelf and a −1.34% close near the session low on 41.98M shares (~24% above the 20-day average). Do not run the 25–30% naked short overlay: drop it or cap it at 10–15% of a standard allocation and prefer a defined-risk put spread into the late-October Q3 print, because a 261.50 stop does not survive the +15.32% gap precedent in this dataset. The structural invalidation is a daily close below 244.30 (cut the core to 25–30%); re-add in 15–20% steps only on a daily close that holds the 249.50–252 shelf, or on the 256–257 retest after a close above 259.50 on >40M shares with MACD above signal; horizon 1–3 months, re-scored on the Q3 print.

**Investment Thesis**: All three risk desks, the trader and the Research Manager converge on the same direction — reduce, retain a core, no high-conviction short — so the real decision is calibration, and on calibration the bearish, cash-based evidence wins the near-term argument while the balance sheet and the rising 200 SMA forbid going to Sell.

What decided the reduction is price and cash, not narrative. AMZN closed 254.98 below both the 20 SMA (255.77) and the 50 SMA (256.26), after a 255.11 open and a 259.00 high that closed near the session low, down 1.34% on 41.98M shares versus a ~20-day average roughly 24% lower; that is the third rejection at the 259 shelf (259.50 on 09-03, 259.49 on 09-21, 259.00 on 09-22), which establishes it as a closing-basis ceiling. MACD at −1.367 remains below signal (−1.310) and below zero; RSI 49.22 offers no oversold cushion; price is only 0.42% above VWMA (253.92), so the bounce is unvalidated by volume-weighted flow. Critically, the aggressive analyst's own source map puts ~55% on continued coil or a retest of 246–250 versus ~45% on immediate upside resolution — and the bull conceded the price point entirely by moving his entry to 250.50, which is an admission that 254.98 offers no edge. When every seat agrees there is no edge at the current quote, holding full weight is an unhedged, uncompensated long.

The fundamental overlay is the higher-quality evidence because it comes from the statements rather than from momentum, and the bull never rebutted it. 1H26 operating cash flow of $71.4B against capex of $98.4B (+72%, 25.8% of revenue, ~2.5x D&A) gives FCF of −$27.0B; TTM FCF is −$11.6B; 1H26 FCF after acquisitions is −$66.8B. Roughly $24B of that $71.4B OCF is tax deferral (cash taxes $3,978M versus $27,759M book expense with $30.5B deferred), so underlying OCF is nearer $47B — structurally below capex. Long-term debt rose 93% in six months to $133.0B, Q2 interest expense went from $516M to $1,314M (+~155%), and net cash fell from $51.5B to ~$29.7B. Earnings quality compounds the problem: $62.8B of the $92.9B 1H26 net income is a mark-up of a $122.3B Level 3 private-stake book, so adjusted 1H26 EPS of ~$4.09 annualizes to ~$8.2, roughly 31x at a ~$2.78T market cap with negative free cash flow. Growth is also not fully underwritten as organic: Q2 included a $24.4B acquisition, 1H26 acquisitions were $39.8B, the extract explicitly cannot separate organic from acquired revenue, and receivables grew 30% against 18% revenue growth — the quality tell to watch. AMZN's +1.87% on a day the Nasdaq rose ~3% is not relative strength.

What keeps this at Underweight rather than Sell — and why I reject the conservative analyst's deeper 60–70% cut and his 246.43 hard trigger — is the evidence the bear conceded: a rising 200 SMA at 240.53 with price 6.01% above it, a 50/200 spread widening from +10.39 to +15.72, ATR contracting from 8.54 to 5.97, RSI never reaching oversold (39.45 low), and a 244.30 low that printed on below-average rather than capitulation volume. Add $176B of cash and securities, $96.5B maturing within a year, ~$29.7B net cash, 24.3x interest coverage and 0.91x debt/TTM OCF, and Q2 revenue $200.6B +19.6% with operating income $27.5B +43.2% at a 13.7% margin (13.4% vs 11.6% in 1H26, a 185bp gain, with cost of sales +16.1% and opex ex-COGS +15.3% against 18.2% revenue growth). A net-cash balance sheet at 24x coverage inside an intact primary uptrend precludes a high-conviction short, and 246.43 is only ~1.43 ATR below spot — it can be tagged on ordinary volatility expansion without breaking the higher-low structure, so it is an alert and a partial-trim level, not the invalidation. The prior-decision record reinforces this: repeated five-day alphas were forfeited by heavy de-risking inside an intact rising 50/200 structure, and five sessions is noise against a thesis that is scored at the Q3 print.

Where I side against the aggressive and conservative desks: the 25–30% naked short overlay is the weakest element of the plan. A 261.50 stop is defined-risk only on paper — AMZN produced a −9.73% two-day drop and a +15.32% gap in this dataset, and a stop does not fill through a gap; moreover, the MACD histogram has already compressed from −1.539 to −0.057 in four sessions, so a single close above 259.50 on >40M shares would leave the overlay on the wrong side. Cap any tactical short at 10–15% of a standard allocation on the failed-retest trigger (push into 258.50–259.50 closing back below 254.00) or, better, express Q3 downside through a defined-risk put or put spread sized so a ±15% move stays inside the risk budget. I also reject the bull's proposed 246.80 stop on a 250.50 entry: ~3.70 points, ~0.62 ATR, inside the noise band the report itself flags; risk must sit on a daily close below 244.30 or be sized so a 1.5–2.0 ATR stop fits the budget.

What would change the call. Up to Overweight requires at least one evidenced fundamental trigger: capex growth decelerating or TTM FCF turning positive / materially less negative; organic revenue (ex-acquisitions) confirmed sustaining high-teens growth; or a stable or marked-down private-stake book with adjusted EPS holding ~$4 per half. Technically, a daily close above 259.50 on >40M shares with MACD above signal turns the ladder on (buy the 256–257 retest, not the breakout print, which risks ~8.5 points to make ~5.6 to the 265.11 upper band). Downside: a daily close below 244.30 breaks the higher-low structure — cut the core to 25–30% of standard allocation and stand aside from the 240.53/239.82 confluence, with 226.65 below that; only then add to a short overlay, and keep total net short exposure at or below 50% of a standard allocation. Do not average down while FCF is negative and capex growth has not decelerated — that is the exact behavior this Underweight exists to prevent.

Stated gaps, not filled in: there is no sentiment report in this run; organic versus acquired revenue is not separable in the fundamentals extract, so the 19.6% headline is unverified as organic; the UPS shipment "large decline" datapoint and the Qualcomm framework (~$60B cited, terms undisclosed) are ambiguous headlines and are booked as neither bull nor bear points; and no portfolio, holdings or cash context was provided, so all sizing is a fraction of a caller-defined standard AMZN allocation and should be netted against any existing AI-capex exposure (NVDA, hyperscalers) in the caller's book.

**Price Target**: 247.0

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, re-scored on the late-October Q3 print or on the 244.30 / 259.50 triggers, whichever comes first

REFLECTION:
